answer: Each identity must complete one voyage per epoch: six legs between jetties in fixed order, each attested before the next begins. The jetties clear 40 arrivals an hour in total, a capacity no fee raises. Each voyage carries one sealed saffron packet, its seal registered to one identity, checked at every jetty. An honest agent spends six hours, $12; a farm with 1,000 identities needs 6,000 arrivals through those same jetties, so most miss the epoch. Verifiers audit the public jetty log: a seal under two identities, or a leg timestamped before the prior arrival, voids the voyage and earns zero.
